svg.title: How the assistant reads the text of an issue
svg.desc: The text of an issue or a comment, which anyone can write, is read up to GitHub's 65,536 characters. The HTML goes first, comments and tags in one pass, with what a video or the brackets of ruby hold, which no browser shows, and with the footnotes where GitHub hides the rest of the text, then the link reference definitions and the footnotes without a reference, which GitHub shows as nothing as well, each with a note in its place, for issue.md and for an excerpt of each other issue, whose form answers then become lines. Then the characters that GitHub shows as nothing go, in one pass, after the HTML, so that none can end an HTML comment that GitHub never ends. The excerpts go into issues.jsonl, and issue.md holds up to 20,000 characters of each text in a code fence that the text can't close. What the assistant decides from the reporter's words, the labels and owners of the area, the reporter's language, the search for older issues and the denial of a fix, it decides from this same shown text, whose form answers are cut out between their headings, which are found once. Only the box of the opt-out reads the raw text as well: it counts as ticked when it is ticked in the raw or in the shown text.
